identity.wikipedia: Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral

land.text: 'the provinces of Udine, Gorizia, Trieste, Pula (Pola), Rijeka (Fiume) and Ljubljana (Lubiana)': the three Italian provinces (Udine as the 1943 province, 'today the provinces of Udine and Pordenone'), Istria for Pola, a 30 km circle for Fiume and Kvarner, a 45 km circle for the Province of Ljubljana (the gazetteer has no Kvarner and no Carniolan province)

predecessors.note: Italian provinces and the Italian-annexed Province of Ljubljana, left without Italian authority after the armistice of 8 September 1943.

land.text: the Italian provinces (Udine, Gorizia, Trieste); the Yugoslav Partisans held Istria, Fiume and Ljubljana

successors.note: The page gives no division. The Partisans' 4th Army engaged the German units and Yugoslav troops withdrew from Trieste from 11 June 1945; the Free Territory of Trieste is not on the page.

capitals.name: Trieste
capitals.note: 'The capital of the zone was the city of Trieste.'

rulers.name: Friedrich Rainer
rulers.title: Reich Defense Commissioner (Supreme Commissioner)
rulers.note: Infobox '1943–1945: Friedrich Rainer'; 'was appointed Reich Defense Commissioner of OZAK'; no appointment date on the page.

correction.text: 'the provinces of Udine, Gorizia, Trieste, Pula (Pola), Rijeka (Fiume) and Ljubljana (Lubiana)': the three Italian provinces (Udine as the 1943 province, 'today the provinces of Udine and Pordenone'), Istria for Pola, a 30 km circle for Fiume and Kvarner, a 45 km circle for the Province of Ljubljana (the gazetteer has no Kvarner and no Carniolan province)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no shape for the zone (its Kingdom of Italy row is 455,534 km2 in 1943, 267 km2 in 1944 and 289,198 km2 in 1945). The page gives no area and no population (page silent); the resolved spec is about 19,500 km2 with Pordenone, which the page counts in the 1943 Province of Udine ('today the provinces of Udine and Pordenone'; added by the eu-21-x reviewer, 2026-11-01; without it neither this zone nor the Italian Social Republic drew Pordenone); the Ljubljana and Fiume circles are guesses, and the modern Gorizia and Trieste provinces are smaller than those of 1943 (the Slovenian Littoral is only partly covered by the Ljubljana circle). It is not part of the Italian Social Republic's shape: the page says 'Both operational zones were separate from the Italian Social Republic (RSI)', although the RSI page footnote says they were 'still formally part' of it.

region.text: 'the provinces of Udine, Gorizia, Trieste, Pula (Pola), Rijeka (Fiume) and Ljubljana (Lubiana)': the three Italian provinces (Udine as the 1943 province, 'today the provinces of Udine and Pordenone'), Istria for Pola, a 30 km circle for Fiume and Kvarner, a 45 km circle for the Province of Ljubljana (the gazetteer has no Kvarner and no Carniolan province)

ledger.note: 10 September 1943: Germany sets up the Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral. 'OZAK was established, with its headquarters in Trieste, on 10 September 1943'; 'It comprised the provinces of Udine, Gorizia, Trieste, Pula (Pola), Rijeka (Fiume) and Ljubljana (Lubiana)'. The Province of Ljubljana 'was given a Slovenian provincial administration' under Rupnik, appointed 22 September 1943.

region.text: the zone under German civil administration, attached to the Gau of Carinthia

ledger.note: 10 September 1943: the zone is attached to the Gau of Carinthia. 'The OZAK was not incorporated in the German Reich outright, but attached to the Gau of Carinthia.'

region.text: 'the provinces of Udine, Gorizia, Trieste, Pula (Pola), Rijeka (Fiume) and Ljubljana (Lubiana)': the three Italian provinces (Udine as the 1943 province, 'today the provinces of Udine and Pordenone'), Istria for Pola, a 30 km circle for Fiume and Kvarner, a 45 km circle for the Province of Ljubljana (the gazetteer has no Kvarner and no Carniolan province)

ledger.note: 2 May 1945: the German units in the zone surrender. 'On 28 April 1945, the San Sabba camp ceased operating'; 'On 30 April 1945, several thousand volunteers of the Italian anti-fascist Comitato di Liberazione Nazionale rose up against the Nazis'; 'On 1 May, Globocnik was given command of a chaotic assortment of German and collaborationist troops'; the units were engaged by the Partisans' 4th Army and surrendered to the New Zealand 2nd Division on 2 May. 'The Partisans began to withdraw from areas west of the Isonzo river on 15 May.'

region.text: 'the provinces of Udine, Gorizia, Trieste, Pula (Pola), Rijeka (Fiume) and Ljubljana (Lubiana)': the three Italian provinces (Udine as the 1943 province, 'today the provinces of Udine and Pordenone'), Istria for Pola, a 30 km circle for Fiume and Kvarner, a 45 km circle for the Province of Ljubljana (the gazetteer has no Kvarner and no Carniolan province)

ledger.note: May 1945: the Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral ends. Infobox 'Dissolution: 1945', with no day; the German units surrendered on 2 May. 'On 11 June Yugoslav troops began to withdraw from Trieste.'

certainty.note: The zone is defined by named Italian provinces, whose boundaries were fixed; the lines of the Pula, Rijeka and Ljubljana provinces are not given on the page.

sources.title: Operational Zone of the Adriatic Littoral
sources.note: Establishment 10 September 1943, six provinces, Trieste capital, Rainer, attached to the Gau of Carinthia, final weeks April-June 1945. No area or population.

sources.title: Operational Zone of the Alpine Foothills
sources.note: Twin zone; 'Both operational zones were separate from the Italian Social Republic'.

notes: Cliopatria lacks the zone. The RSI page's footnote ('still formally part of the RSI') and the zone pages ('separate from the RSI') disagree; the italian-social-republic shape leaves the zone out. The page has no area, population, Rainer appointment date, or formal end date; 2 May 1945 comes from the surrender of the German units. The Free Territory of Trieste (1947-1954) is not on the page. Region names the gazetteer lacks: none (Kvarner/Fiume and the Province of Ljubljana are circles, a 'Province of Ljubljana' and 'Kvarner' region would be better).
